newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman honeymoon fading in Nicaragua, poll shows.
newsitem.headline: Aleman honeymoon fading in Nicaragua, poll shows.

text.p: Nicaraguans are increasingly pessimistic about the future of their country and disillusioned with President Arnoldo Aleman's right-wing government, according to a CID-Gallup poll released on Thursday.
In the poll, 50 percent of those surveyed thought Nicaragua was "on the wrong road," while 30 percent thought it had chosen the right path and was doing well.
This is a reversal of what CID-Gallup polled shortly after Aleman's election when 50 percent of those surveyed thought the country had chosen the right path.

The poll also showed that the vast majority of Nicaraguans -- 87 percent -- say they have seen no positive changes since Aleman came to power, especially in terms of unemployment, which they overwhelming said was the country's main problem.
Carlos Denton, president of CID-Gallup Costa Rica, said the growing discontent could lead to problems for Aleman if he failed to meet the high expectations he created in his election campaign.
"Unemployment is Nicaragua's principal problem and if he doesn't reduce this problem discontent is going to rise," Denton said.
Despite the growing disillusionment with his government, Aleman himself was not blamed by most of those polled.
While 38 percent said Aleman was doing a "good" or "very good" job, 28 percent said he was doing a "bad" or "very bad" job. Aleman was elected with 51 percent of the vote.
The CID-Gallup poll surveyed 1,248 people across Nicaragua between April 10 and 18 with a margin for error of 2.8 percent.
Part of the polling was done during a five-day national strike by pro-Sandinista unions and grassroots groups that represented the first major challenge to Aleman's government.
Denton said the strike did not affect the poll's results.
